data.one_liner: Wrapper around ReorderableListView that adds tree structure, expand/collapse, and reordering.
data.what_it_does: It lets you build a list of items that can be expanded or collapsed like a tree, while still supporting drag‑to‑reorder. Each item is built via a builder that receives the current model and child widget. The package removes the visibility_detector dependency, so visibility must be handled manually if needed.
use_when: You need a reorderable list with expandable/collapsible tree nodes.
You want to reuse ReorderableListView API but add hierarchical support.
You need a simple, declarative way to build custom list items with drag handles.
avoid_when: You only need a flat list or a simple ListView.
You require high‑performance scrolling for very large trees.
You need built‑in visibility detection for lazy loading.
strengths: Easy integration with existing ReorderableListView code.
No extra code generation or build_runner steps.
Supports custom builders and drag handles out of the box.
weaknesses: Visibility detection removed; must wrap items manually if needed.
Limited to the features of ReorderableListView; no advanced animations or custom drag logic.
No support for nested lists beyond a single tree level.
